LESSON: AREA

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 3.6: Area

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Area. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify surfaces of different objects in the environment
2. cover the area of different surfaces of objects using smaller objects
3. appreciate different surfaces in the environment

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify surfaces of different objects in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify surfaces of different objects in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. cover the area of different surfaces of objects using smaller objects
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to cover the area of different surfaces of objects using smaller objects. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. appreciate different surfaces in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate different surfaces in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Area.
2. Explain Area to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.

5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Area. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Area important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
